step2_join_waitlist._note: IMPORTANT for the adapter: a waitlist reservation's `spot` object comes back with all-empty/null fields (not omitted, not null itself — an object with empty string ids). waitlist_position stays null even after joining on this tenant; don't rely on it for UI display. available_spot_count stayed 0 (unaffected by waitlist join, as expected).

step3_cancel_penalty_check_for_waitlist._note: Same cancel_penalty endpoint works for waitlist reservations, not just standard bookings.

step4_leave_waitlist._note: CRITICAL for the adapter's status-mapping: leaving a waitlist sets status to "removed", NOT "standard cancel" (which is what a normal booking cancel produces — see prod-cancel-flow.json). These are two distinct terminal statuses depending on reservation_type. Oddly, is_user_waitlisted remains true on the embedded class_session snapshot in this particular response even after leaving — likely a stale snapshot in that specific response rather than live state; don't trust that field on a cancel response, re-fetch the class/reservation to confirm current state.
